conflicts.point: Whether parameter caps and export restrictions on model weights effectively prevent the proliferation of dangerous capabilities or merely constitute unenforceable regulatory theater.

positions.stance: Export controls and infrastructure choke points effectively govern dual-use diffusion by intercepting models at centralized training nodes.
Peer-to-peer distribution and commodity hardware execution bypass export controls entirely, rendering parameter caps completely ineffective.

conflicts.point: Whether centralized pre-deployment certification boards are necessary for AI accountability or function primarily as anticompetitive regulatory capture mechanisms.

positions.stance: Structured pre-market certification is necessary to prevent irreversible dual-use hazards before unverified models are released.
Sector-specific post-market enforcement under existing statutory authorities provides sufficient accountability without erecting monopolistic barriers to entry.
